approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph-based genetic algorithm whose offspring are chosen by Gaussian-process Thompson sampling. Each round it breeds a fresh pool of 160 candidate molecules from the best molecules found so far. Breeding parents come mostly from the top score quantiles, and offspring are made by joining connected fragments of two parents or by short chains of atom, bond and ring edits. Duplicates are rejected, and so are offspring that introduce a new out-of-envelope sulfur environment. A Gaussian process is trained on every scored molecule of the session, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a Tanimoto-type similarity, and it predicts the whole pool. Ten correlated samples are drawn from its posterior; each picks its best remaining candidate, and those ten molecules are scored. The results flow back into the training set and into a 64-molecule elite population.
approach.novelty: This arm deliberately adds no new search behaviour. It is a placebo control for the stall trigger tested in the previous round. The run counts consecutive rounds of ten that fail to beat its best score. Whenever that count reaches three, it draws one extra set of random numbers from the selector's random generator and throws it away before the usual draw. Every rule, probability and pool size stays exactly as in the Parent, so from that moment on only the selector's luck changes. The earlier siblings at the same trigger each changed a real rule during stalls: wider sampling noise, a four-times larger candidate pool, longer mutation walks, or no crossover. They moved the five-task, three-seed average by between -0.014 and +0.008. This arm measures how far that average moves when only chance changes at the same moment. Those results, and this round's companion arm that rescales the sampling noise during stalls, can then be judged against it.

observed_bottleneck: The sulfur-gated Anchor n-1744a1494180 (complete panel mean 0.596453, SD 0.033970) has no measured reference for the stall-gated deltas now being read against it. Recomputing the shared K=3 counter from its own published trajectories gives 91 stalled announced batches in 29 episodes over 13 of 15 sessions. deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never stall. The first stalled batch begins at evaluation 41 (zaleplon s0, median_2 s0), 61 (zaleplon s2), 71 (sitagliptin s1), 81 (zaleplon s1, median_2 s2), 121 (sitagliptin s0), 151 (deco_hop s1, drd2 s1), 171 (sitagliptin s2), 181 (median_2 s1), 191 (drd2 s2) and 231 (drd2 s0). The four round-38 arms at this trigger (n-189cd716f027 -0.009718, n-e5dba2059cfe +0.007648, n-25b9a57765d8 +0.004664, n-9e5f01d67b9f -0.014192) first leave the Anchor trajectory in exactly those batches: the first differing evaluation equals the list above for n-e5dba2059cfe and n-9e5f01d67b9f and lies at most five evaluations later for the other two. Afterwards only 2.3 to 6.1 percent of their accepted molecules occur anywhere in the Anchor's same session (53/2340, 55/2340, 74/2335, 142/2320, recomputed from the published trajectories). Every gated delta is therefore a contrast between two essentially disjoint post-trigger paths, and nobody has measured how large such a contrast is when no law changes. Their allocator random numbers never desynchronized. The logged standard normals of n-189cd716f027 (zaleplon seed 0) and n-e5dba2059cfe (sitagliptin seed 1) equal the Anchor's in all 29 batches, so all of their divergence ran through changed pools and states. The four arms span 0.021840 on dependent seeds. The exact same-state first stalled batch does not order them: the Anchor's summed increment is 0.165561, and the smallest increment (0.125805) belongs to the largest delta. Both gains take their largest cell from sitagliptin seed 1, a cell that unrelated departures from this Anchor usually raise. The catalog record for sampled residual influence states that only a neutral same-algorithm trajectory-perturbation control on this Anchor and seeds could size component effects. The allocator stream is a consequential place to perturb: on this Anchor, removing the sampled residual (n-f04cec6ab705) cost 0.116317. The gate must sit at the same trigger: the always-on four-times pool (n-da0eeecfb462, -0.016060) differs from its stall-only version mainly by the two deco_hop sessions that a gated design never changes. The registered presence question for ordinary continuation (n-c070e95b09ef, -0.030700) waits on the same control. The proxy-versus-gain caution from n-9f11b684e560 applies to any favourable proxy this arm shows.

adoptions.applicability: This applies to this node because the open question is how large a panel delta the K=3 trigger produces when nothing but the random path changes. The unchanged-algorithm contrast is that quantity, specialized to the exact divergence point of the gated siblings.
adoptions.borrowed_element: A seed-only comparison of an unchanged algorithm (same configuration, only the random realization differs) used as the reference for how large a difference randomness alone produces between runs.

deviations.adopted_setting: One paired realization per protocol Search seed (0/1/2) on each of five tasks. Each is identical to the Anchor until the session's first K=3 stalled batch and differs afterwards only in the allocator's realized random stream. One fifteen-cell panel delta is read through the bound interpretation rule, with no significance claim.
deviations.paper_setting: Ten whole-run trials differing only in the random seed, averaged in two groups of five and compared by a two-sample t-test over learning curves.
deviations.reason: Seeds, budget and panel are protocol-owned, and the window's question is the path divergence produced at the exact trigger the gated siblings share. The reference must therefore share their prefix and trigger rather than redraw whole runs.

deviations.adopted_setting: Only the posterior allocator's generator is perturbed, and only from the trigger onward. The breeding generator diverges solely as a consequence of different selected molecules.
deviations.paper_setting: A new seed perturbs every random source of the run from the start (environment, initialization and exploration).
deviations.reason: This keeps the perturbation at the component and moment the round-38 law changes act on, keeps it auditable as law-free, and protects the deco_hop sessions that never stall. A breeding-stream reference remains open.

adoptions.implementation_change: Candidate optimize.py, FingerprintPosterior.select: when the Evolution's K=3 stall counter is active, one torch.randn of the inherited (batch size, pool size) float64 shape is drawn from the selector's own generator after the pool Cholesky and discarded before the inherited allocation draw. The trigger bookkeeping in Evolution.suggest and Evolution.observe is copied from the round-38 stall-only pool arm, and all laws are unchanged.

literature_review.conclusion: The seed-variance literature supports measuring a law-free random-realization contrast as the reference for differences between variants of a stochastic method. It also warns that a few realizations can differ substantially by chance, but it supplies no magnitude for this benchmark. The specific design, one discarded allocator block per stalled batch at the shared K=3 trigger, comes from internal evidence: the Curate open question on stall-gated path divergence and the m-000000000006 catalog condition. The A/A-test query returned only book listings and no readable source text, so nothing is adopted from it.

sources.applicability: This is a direct methodological analog: an unchanged algorithm that differs only in its random realization is the reference for how large an outcome difference randomness alone produces. Its benchmark, numbers and statistical procedure are not campaign evidence. Here the analog is applied to one adaptive molecular search with a shared prefix and a single perturbation point.
sources.finding: In 'Random Seeds and Trials' the authors run 10 trials of one hyperparameter configuration, 'only varying the random seed across all 10 trials', split them into two sets of five, and report that 'the variance between runs is enough to create statistically different distributions just from varying random seeds' (TRPO on HalfCheetah-v1, two-sample t-test t=-9.0916, p=0.0016).
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning that Matters, Henderson, Islam, Bachman, Pineau, Precup and Meger, AAAI 2018 (ar5iv full text of arXiv 1709.06560)

sources.applicability: Supports this arm's stated limit. It randomizes one source (the allocator stream after the trigger) in one realization per cell, so it measures a single draw of path noise rather than its spread. A generator-stream perturbation and further seeds would be additional sources of variance. No procedure from the paper is implemented.
sources.finding: Modelling the whole benchmarking process, the authors find that variance due to data sampling, parameter initialization and hyperparameter choice markedly impacts results. They also find that an estimator randomizing more sources of variation comes closer to the ideal estimator, at a 51-fold reduction in compute cost.
sources.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks, Bouthillier et al., MLSys 2021 (arXiv 2103.03098)

hypothesis: Neutral path-divergence control at the shared K=3 stall trigger. In each announced batch allocated while the session's own consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter is at least 3, draw one standard-normal array of the inherited allocation shape (announced batch size by pool size, float64) from the posterior selector's own seeded generator and discard it immediately before the inherited correlated Thompson draw. That batch and every later allocation then consume the next unused blocks of the same i.i.d. stream. No law, probability, scale, threshold, pool size, operator or gate changes; only the realized random path departs from the Anchor at the trigger.

finding_summary.headline: Pure path-noise control at the stall trigger ran exactly: panel moved -0.0017, but single cells swung from -0.034 to +0.041
finding_summary.insights:
Under the interpretation rule fixed before the run, a reference delta within plus or minus 0.002 means the two round-38 stall-gated gains stand above a single path realization: +0.0076 for longer mutation walks during stalls and +0.0047 for a fourfold candidate pool during stalls. That is the registered answer. The run itself gives three reasons to hold it loosely.

First, the near-zero panel mean is a cancellation. Changing nothing but luck moved single cells by up to 0.04 and seed macros by -0.013 to +0.008. That seed-level spread of 0.021 is as wide as the whole span of the four round-38 panel deltas (0.022). Averaging three seeds narrows noise at the panel level, but one panel cannot show by how much. Leaving out one cell puts the reference anywhere between -0.005 and +0.001. One null panel is a single draw from the path-noise distribution, not its width, so the margin by which +0.0047 clears it is not a calibrated margin.

Second, the cell both gated gains lean on, sitagliptin seed 1, fell by 0.018 under pure re-drawing, while sitagliptin seed 2 rose by 0.041. A gain at sitagliptin seed 1 is therefore not an automatic by-product of leaving the Anchor's path at the trigger. Swings of a few hundredths in single cells, in either direction, are.

Third, proxies drift with no rule change. This control lost 24 parent-beating offspring and 0.37 of positive parent-gain mass, so proxy differences of that order between arms are within what a re-draw alone produces and cannot be read as mechanism.

The exact same-state first stalled batch is now calibrated as well. The Anchor's draw and this re-draw are two independent samples of the same rule on the same state, and they agree closely: 0.166 and 0.158, with nine offspring beating the best score in each. The first-batch increments of 0.126 to 0.166 in the longer-walk, crossover-off and wider-noise arms sit at this noise level. The fourfold-pool arm's 0.268, with 15 such offspring, stands apart from both draws. That is the clearest same-state sign that one round-38 change did something different at the moment it switched on.

The chemistry assessment is consistent with the size of those cell-level swings. In four of the five objectives the best molecules concentrate on one dominant scaffold, and late progress is largely halogen and substituent permutations on it. Which permutation a re-drawn path happens to reach can therefore decide a cell's endpoint by a few hundredths.

Still open: a reference that perturbs the breeding random stream rather than the allocator's, and repeated reference arms or more seeds to estimate the spread of the panel delta rather than one draw of it. This reference also does not calibrate Children that leave the Anchor from the first batch, such as the continuation removal (-0.031) or the always-on fourfold pool (-0.016). Those also give up the deco_hop seed-0 realization that a gated design never touches, so they would need an ungated neutral control. The route's review conditions end this arm with this one panel. The companion stall-time noise-contraction arm should be read against it, and recorded as unidentified if its delta falls inside this reference.
finding_summary.results:
The control behaved exactly as registered, so its score is a valid reference. Thirteen of fifteen sessions reached the stall trigger, the same thirteen as the Anchor. The two deco_hop sessions on seeds 0 and 2 never stalled and reproduced the Anchor record for record, including its 0.856 deco_hop seed-0 endpoint. Over all 435 announced batches the logged stall counter matched a recomputation from the run's own scores. The extra random block was drawn and thrown away in exactly the 104 stalled batches (32 stall episodes, against the Anchor's 91 batches in 29) and in no other batch. Every session matched the Anchor in every scored molecule and every logged internal step up to its first stalled batch. At that batch, in all thirteen sessions, the candidate pool and its predicted means and uncertainties were identical to the Anchor's. The thrown-away block was bit-for-bit the block the Anchor had used, and replaying the Anchor's rule on it reproduced the Anchor's ten picks, while the run's own picks differed. From there the search left the Anchor's path. Every one of the 104 stalled batches picked differently from its same-state replay, with on average 6.3 of 10 molecules different. Only 83 of 2,337 molecules scored after divergence (3.6%) also appear in the Anchor's session, inside the 2.3 to 6.1% of the round-38 stall-gated arms. The selection rule itself did not move. The shift in where picks fell on the predicted-mean and uncertainty rankings gave test statistics of -1.45 and +1.24, far inside the 3.26 bound. Every pool held 160 candidates and no batch fell back to the backup route.

On the score panel the matched mean went from 0.596453 to 0.594718, a reference delta of -0.001735. Seed macros moved by -0.0127, -0.0006 and +0.0080. Under that small mean the individual cells moved a lot. On the down side, zaleplon seed 0 fell 0.034, sitagliptin seed 1 0.018, sitagliptin seed 0 0.013 and drd2 seed 0 0.010. On the up side, sitagliptin seed 2 rose 0.041, zaleplon seed 1 0.009, median_2 seed 1 0.005 and drd2 seed 2 0.004. Five cells rose, eight fell and the two never-stalled cells were exactly unchanged. The population SD of the fifteen cell deltas was 0.0154, and the thirteen cells the gate can reach average -0.0020. Dropping any single cell moves the reference anywhere from -0.0048 (without sitagliptin seed 2) to +0.0006 (without zaleplon seed 0). Re-drawing the exact same state at each session's first stalled batch gave a summed incumbent gain of 0.158, against the Anchor's 0.166. Both had nine offspring beating the best score held at announcement, with batch mean scores of 0.334 and 0.339. Across the whole run the gain proxies drifted slightly down although no rule changed. Positive gain over the best parent was 16.88 against 17.25, parent-beating offspring numbered 624 against 648, and mean offspring score was 0.3700 against 0.3720. Incumbent gain inside stalls was 0.579 over 104 stalled batches against 0.477 over 91. Both runs broke a stall in about 28% of stalled batches.

molecular.headline: Flat, ring-rich, heavily halogenated aromatics whose best scorers reach their scores through N-F, O-F, fused 4-rings and aminals.
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 4350 molecules (870 per task, 860-868 of them unique canonical structures per task), and they are a consistent chemical type: medium-sized flat polyaromatics of 24-32 heavy atoms and 345-490 Da, carrying 3.4-4.3 rings and 2.1-3.5 aromatic rings each. The digest counters agree: ring_closure_rate 0.959-0.981 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.948-0.972, so ring and aromatic chemistry is genuinely abundant, not an artifact of my reading. Three absences hold on every objective without exception. No molecule carries a formal charge (digest charged_rate 0.000 on all five). No molecule declares stereochemistry (digest stereocentre_rate 0.000 on all five), although RDKit finds 0.35-1.94 unassigned sp3 stereocentres per molecule, so the generator proposes stereocentres and never resolves them. And no molecule anywhere contains a trifluoromethyl group - 0 of 4350 - even where the score climbs monotonically with fluorine count. What varies between tasks is only the decoration: halogen_rate is 0.806-0.982 on four objectives and 0.140 on the fifth, and that one is also the only objective whose top molecules are free of halogen-on-heteroatom motifs. The 30 seed molecules each session starts from are ordinary drug-like matter (SA 2.99, QED 0.517, and not one of the 30 carries a heteroatom-halogen bond, a C-nitroso group, a fused 3- or 4-membered ring or an aminal). The optimizer leaves that space as the score rises: synthetic-accessibility score goes to 3.3-4.6 in the 50 highest scorers, and 68 to 100 percent of those top 50 carry at least one of those motifs on four of the five objectives. The search is also narrow where it matters. Proposals are nominally almost all distinct, but the 50 highest scorers collapse to 9-12 distinct Murcko scaffolds on four objectives, with a single scaffold covering 19-29 of them, and four molecules on one objective share the score 0.4405 while differing only by Br/Cl and F/Br swaps on one core. Finally, 106 of the 4350 proposals have three or fewer heavy atoms - single atoms and diatomics such as C, Cl, FBr, FF and NSF - and all but a handful scored zero. On comparison: context.comparison reports child_complete true and paired_complete true against Parent n-1744a1494180 on seeds 0, 1, 2, and all 15 Parent trajectory files exist and were read. The Parent's chemistry is the same chemistry. On one objective its seed-0 and seed-2 trajectories are identical to this node's in all 300 records, and the other 13 sessions first differ at evaluation 41-231; motif rates track within a few points, the visible exceptions being N-O single bonds (Parent 17.7 vs this node 2.3 percent of proposals on one objective, 25.4 vs 5.9 on another) and N-N single bonds (Parent 34.6 vs 10.7 on a third). I describe that difference and do not interpret it; score and activation are not mine to judge.

per_task.generated_character: Small flat tricyclics of about 25 heavy atoms and 345-406 Da: a 5-6 fused azaindole or indole bearing a 2-carboxanilide, with methyl, ethyl and methoxy decoration and a halogen on almost every available position. Mean 3.38 rings and 2.26 aromatic rings; 82.9 percent of proposals contain an amide and 75.3 percent an aryl halide; pyridine appears in 20.3 percent, nitrile in only 3.1 percent and pyrimidine in 0.3 percent. The digest counters show halogen_rate 0.908 and mean SMILES length 43.7, the shortest of the five tasks. Scores span 0.0 to 0.4828 with median 0.31734.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-bromo amides in the single best molecule and in 34 of the top 50; these are oxidants, not stable amides
N-halogenated ring nitrogen (n2F) on essentially every high scorer, a motif with no stable analogue
N-hydroxy amide and O-halogen bonds in the lower set, e.g. CCc1c(C)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)N(O)c1ccccn1)n2F at 0.4520
dearomatized azepine tautomers among the final molecules, e.g. CCN1C=c2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccccc3)cc2=C(Cl)C=C1Br
25 proposals of three or fewer heavy atoms, including NSF and Cl, each scoring 0.0
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl or other fluorinated methyl on carbon anywhere in the 870 proposals, despite halogen_rate 0.908
aromatic nitrile is nearly absent (3.1 percent of proposals, 1 of the top 50) although it is present in the seed matter
fused diazine bicyclics such as pyrazolopyrimidine are unreachable; pyrimidine appears in 0.3 percent of proposals
tertiary amides whose nitrogen substituent is a carbon group rather than a halogen are rare in the top set
no basic amine on the high scorers (1.4 percent of the top quartile) although the Parent reaches 10.6 percent of proposals
polar surface area falls as score rises (47.6 in the top 50 against 54.6 across proposals), so no polar decoration is retained
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards piling halogen onto the indole/anilide core, including onto its nitrogens. Mean score rises from 0.241 at zero halogens to 0.338 at three. 33.6 percent of all proposals put a halogen on a ring nitrogen and 66 percent of the top 50 do; N-halogenated amide nitrogen is in 35.9 percent of proposals and 53.0 percent of the top quartile. Matched pairs in the trajectories make the local effect explicit: CCc1c(C)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)N(F)c1ccccc1)n2F scores 0.4405 while its plain secondary amide CCc1c(C)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)Nc1ccccc1)n2F scores 0.3923, and the N-Br analogue scores the same 0.4405 as the N-F one. The best molecule carries two N-F bonds. Across all 20 such pairs the mean difference is only -0.0031, so this is a local ridge the search found and sat on, not a global preference.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the five tasks: about 32 heavy atoms, 378-487 Da, mean 4.20 rings and 3.50 aromatic rings, TPSA 125, and the longest SMILES in the digest at up to 191 characters. Two distinct families dominate. Seed 0 produced a pentacyclic pyrazolo-fused thioxo-pyrimidinone bearing a quinazoline, and seeds 1 and 2 produced a very different polysubstituted benzene bearing acetyl, formyl, a 2-alkoxyethyl chain and a nitroso-aminal, fused to a strained small carbocycle. 45.7 percent of proposals contain pyridine and 32.9 percent pyrimidine; ketone 22.5 percent, ester 21.6 percent, nitrile 22.5 percent. Scores span 0.5 (an evident floor, hit by single atoms) to 0.8561, median 0.596207.
liabilities: aryl hypofluorite O-F bonds in all three joint-best molecules, a bond that does not survive isolation
fused 4-membered carbocycles on a benzene ring in 84 percent of the top 50, a benzocyclobutadiene-type strain
C-nitroso and nitroso-aminal groups in 41 of the top 50, e.g. COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2
chloromethyl ether and thioester-like C(F)OCCl and OC=S groups on the best molecules, both alkylating or hydrolytically unstable
100 percent of the top 50 carry at least one of these motifs, against 0 of the 30 seed molecules
19 proposals of three or fewer heavy atoms, including C#N at the 0.5 score floor
missing_features: no trifluoromethyl in any of the 870 proposals, and aryl fluoride vanishes entirely from the top 50
sulfonamide never appears in any proposal although the scaffold class normally carries one
basic amine on a saturated ring appears in 3.6 percent of proposals and 0.9 percent of the top quartile
aryl methyl ether drops from 23.7 percent of proposals to 16 percent of the top 50 and no other stable polar linker replaces it
the high scorers reach shape targets with strained small rings instead of ordinary 5- and 6-membered saturated rings
QED falls from 0.303 across proposals to 0.230 in the top 50, so nothing drug-like is retained as score rises
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Two separate ridges, both structural rather than functional. The seed-0 family rewards the fused polycyclic core plus a quinazoline arm and tops out at 0.8561; the seed-1/2 family rewards a specific strained fused arrangement, and 84 percent of the top 50 contain a 4-membered ring while only 22.3 percent of all proposals do, with 82 percent of the top 50 carrying that 4-ring fused into another ring. 41 of the top 50 carry a C-nitroso group against 27.5 percent of all proposals. Aryl fluoride is in 65.6 percent of proposals but 0 percent of the top 50, so halogen on carbon is not what is being rewarded here; O-F rises instead, from 2.4 percent of proposals to 16 percent of the top 50. This is the only objective whose best molecules were reached identically by Parent and node on two of three seeds.

per_task.generated_character: The most conventional-looking and the greasiest set: about 30 heavy atoms, 449 Da in the top 50, mean logP 5.33 overall and 5.55 in the top 50, TPSA down to 29.7 in the top 50. The high scorers are a single recognisable pharmacophore - a 3-chlorophenyl on a quaternary carbon of a 7-membered 1,3-diazepane, N-linked by an ethylene tether to a second, bromo- and alkyl-substituted benzene. per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient rewards a fixed aromatic recognition pair - quinoline plus pyrazole, 98 percent of the top 50 contain pyridine-type nitrogen - decorated with a polar amide/urea ring, and it rewards closing that ring large. Mean score is 0.169 for molecules with no ring of 8 or more atoms and 0.200 for those with one, and 80 percent of the top 50 carry such a ring against 32.8 percent of all proposals. Amide prevalence rises from 37.8 percent in the bottom quartile to 98.2 percent in the top. Hydroxyl and N-O motifs are selected against, falling from 30.0 and 28.6 percent in the bottom quartile to 0.9 and 4.6 percent in the top. This is the one objective where the top 50 is almost free of reactive liabilities, at 2 percent.

per_task.generated_character: The most tightly property-converged and the least plausible set. About 26 heavy atoms, 352-394 Da, mean 3.73 rings and 2.57 aromatic rings. The top molecules are a purine-like fused pyrimidinedione-imine bearing a fluorinated cyclopentene or cyclopropane-fused ring and several fluoroalkyl chains. 91.8 percent of proposals contain a pyrimidine and 100 percent of the top 50 do. Scores span 7.7e-27 to 0.6809, median 0.17084, the lowest median of the five.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks fluorine count almost monotonically: mean 0.039 at zero fluorines, 0.122 at one, 0.213 at two, 0.308 at three and 0.385 at four, with the maximum 0.6809 at four. The gradient therefore rewards loading fluorine while holding lipophilicity near 2.05 and polar surface near 77, and the molecules satisfy it with the only fluorine chemistry this generator can make: 78 percent of the top 50 put fluorine on a ring nitrogen and 70 percent use a fluoromethyl or fluoroethyl chain, while trifluoromethyl occurs in none of the 870. The run also shows the gradient does not reward every N-F: the matched pair CN(F)c1ccccc1-n1c(C2C=CCN2)... at 0.5306 scores 0.0903 below its N-H analogue CNc1ccccc1-n1c(C2C=CCN2)... at 0.6209, so it is ring N-F specifically that the search exploited.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 30 seed molecules any session starts from carries a heteroatom-halogen bond, but across the five objectives 33.6 and 44.0 percent of all proposals put a halogen on a ring nitrogen, and 66 and 78 percent of the 50 highest scorers do. On one objective the single best molecule carries two N-F bonds and on another all three joint-best molecules carry an aryl O-F bond. Matched pairs show the search found a real local ridge there: one core scores 0.4405 as its N-fluoro amide and 0.3923 as the plain secondary amide, the same +0.048 appearing for the N-bromo analogue. Over all 20 such pairs on that objective the mean difference is only -0.0031, and on two other objectives de-halogenating the nitrogen gained 0.0903 and 0.2301, so the generator is not following a consistent signal - it is reaching a narrow ridge through bonds its own starting matter never contains.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator places halogens on nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur as freely as on carbon, and has no rule treating that as a different kind of edit.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom-identity and substituent mutations should treat halogen attachment to N, O or S as a distinct gated edit rather than one more atom swap, or filter it at pool admission the way the existing sulfur-environment gate already filters one motif class. The point is not to forbid the motif but to stop an endpoint being reachable only through it, so that a surrogate fitted on accepted observations stops being taught that halogen-on-heteroatom is the cheapest way up.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Trifluoromethyl occurs in 0 of the 4350 molecules proposed across all five objectives, and CF2 in at most 1.0 percent on any one of them, even though one objective's score rises monotonically with fluorine count - mean 0.039, 0.122, 0.213, 0.308, 0.385 at zero through four fluorines - and 43.0 percent of its proposals carry an alkyl C-F. That objective's best molecules reach four fluorines using two ring N-F bonds, a quaternary C-F and a fluoromethyl chain instead. Sulfonamide is likewise absent from all 870 proposals on one objective and present in only 8.7 percent of another's, and triazole and tetrazole appear in none of the 4350.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot assemble any multi-substituted single-carbon group; every group it builds is one atom per edit, so common polysubstituted carbon groups are unreachable.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The mutation set needs a group-level insertion operator that substitutes a whole chemical group in one edit from a small curated list, instead of requiring three independent single-atom additions that each pass through a lower-scoring intermediate. Without it, any fitness surface rewarding a polysubstituted group is reachable only by partial, less stable imitations, and the intermediate states are selected away before the group completes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Piperazine appears in 0.0 to 1.8 percent of proposals per objective, and morpholine and all-carbon piperidine in none of the 4350. Yet basic nitrogen is clearly rewarded somewhere: on one objective 58.6 percent of proposals and 77.0 percent of the top quartile carry a neutral basic amine, with prevalence rising from 27.7 percent in the bottom quartile. The generator supplies it as a 7-membered 1,3-diazepane whose quaternary benzylic carbon is an N,C,N aminal, present in 76 percent of that objective's 50 highest scorers against 27.9 percent of its proposals - a hydrolytically labile centre rather than a stable ring amine.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds rings by closing whatever chain is available rather than by substituting a known ring, so it cannot place saturated nitrogen heterocycles and supplies basic nitrogen on unstable carbons instead.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add a ring-replacement or ring-insertion operator drawing from a curated set of common saturated heterocycles, so that a basic or polar centre the fitness surface rewards can be installed on a stable ring. The current operators can only reach such a centre by closing a chain around it, which systematically produces aminals, hemiaminals and strained or oversized rings in the molecules that score best.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective 84 percent of the 50 highest scorers contain a 4-membered ring and 82 percent have it fused into another ring, against 22.3 percent of its proposals. On a second, 80 percent of the top 50 contain a ring of 8 or more atoms against 32.8 percent of proposals, and mean score is 0.200 with such a ring against 0.169 without. On a third, 20 percent of the top 50 carry a cyclopropane fused to the aromatic core. None of the 30 seed molecules on any objective contains a fused 3- or 4-membered ring. Ring-size homologues score interchangeably - a 10-membered and an 8-membered version of one core scored 0.2272 and 0.2265 - so size itself is not what the surface rewards.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring closure is unconstrained in size and in fusion, so the generator reaches shape targets through strained three- and four-membered fused rings and through eight- to ten-membered rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The ring-forming and ring-expanding edits need a size and fusion constraint, so that a shape or distance target has to be met with ordinary 5- and 6-membered rings. Because homologues of different ring size score almost identically, constraining size costs the search very little score and removes a whole class of strained and macrocyclic endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.000 on all five objectives, so no proposed SMILES carries a configuration marker. RDKit nevertheless finds 0.35 to 1.94 unassigned sp3 stereocentres per molecule, 1.54 per molecule in one objective's top quartile, and 42.8 percent of another objective's proposals contain a bridged ring system. The generator is therefore proposing molecules whose diastereomers it cannot distinguish and cannot ask about.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never declares stereochemistry, although it routinely proposes sp3 stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation would need stereo-bearing atoms and an operator that sets or inverts configuration at an existing centre. Until then every proposal is a flat graph, any objective sensitive to configuration is unaddressable in principle, and a surrogate fitted on these observations cannot learn a configuration preference it was never shown.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 106 of the 4350 proposals have three or fewer heavy atoms - 13 to 33 per objective - and they are literally C, Cl, F, S, C=C, C#C, FF, FBr, NSF and OCF. On four of the five objectives every one of them scored 0.0 or within 0.013 of it; on the fifth they land on that objective's 0.5 score floor. The same fragments recur across seeds and evaluations, including at evaluations 292 and 293 of 300 on one session, so the degenerate proposals are not confined to early exploration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Mutation can strip a molecule down to one to three heavy atoms and the pool admits the fragment, so some oracle budget goes to single atoms and diatomics.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Pool admission needs a minimum heavy-atom count, and the deletion side of the mutation operators needs a lower size bound, so that offspring cannot collapse below a useful size. The budget recovered is small in percentage terms but it is spent at a point in the run where it buys nothing at all and it feeds the surrogate observations that carry no structural information.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Proposals are nominally almost all distinct - 860 to 868 unique canonical structures out of 870 per objective - but the 50 highest scorers collapse to 9, 10, 12 and 9 distinct Murcko scaffolds on four of the five objectives, with a single scaffold covering 19, 19, 19 and 29 of them. Within one session the top 30 came from 3 scaffolds with one appearing 28 times. Four molecules on one objective share the identical score 0.4405 and differ only by Br/Cl and F/Br swaps on the same core, and three more share 0.4388 the same way. The one objective whose top 50 spans 30 scaffolds is also the one with the narrowest score span.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator explores by re-decorating one scaffold rather than by changing scaffold, so late budget buys halogen permutations of an already-found core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Crossover between two members of a converged population returns the same scaffold, so diversity has to be maintained explicitly: a scaffold-level novelty term in parent selection, or an edit that replaces a ring system wholesale rather than its substituents. Otherwise the proposal distribution narrows to substituent permutations of one core, which is exactly where exact-duplicate rejection still reports almost perfect uniqueness while the chemistry has stopped moving.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An exocyclic C=NH imine on a ring carbon - the minor tautomer of an aromatic amino-heterocycle - is in 50.1 percent of one objective's proposals and 98 percent of its 50 highest scorers. Dearomatized ring forms show up in the final molecules of another objective, such as a 7-membered C=C cross-conjugated ring in place of an aromatic one, and ring thiones are in 13.1 percent of a third's proposals. Separately, the digest charged_rate is 0.000 on all five objectives: no formal charge appears in any of the 4350 molecules, and quaternary ammonium and carboxylate never occur, so basic and acidic centres are always written neutral.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator treats tautomers as distinct molecules and frequently settles on the non-dominant one, and it emits no charged species at all.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Canonicalise tautomers before duplicate checking and before surrogate featurisation, so the pool does not hold several writings of one compound and the surrogate is not fitted on the form a chemist would not draw. The atom vocabulary also has no charged states, which puts zwitterions and permanently charged groups outside the reachable space regardless of how the fitness surface is shaped.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
